Hi Olivia — really appreciate the clear context. I spoke with Product and Legal and sketched a path forward below. Attaching a short redline (proposed-sla-diff.pdf) and a sample monthly calculation spreadsheet (cloudforge-maf-v2.xlsx).

Proposed approach (summary):

1) Two-tier latency SLOs: keep the interactive latency SLO (P95 < 500ms) intact for routed interactive traffic. Introduce a separate "batch processing" SLO (P90 < 5s) for scheduled batch jobs to reflect different workload characteristics.

2) Scheduled batch window offset: allow customers to register recurring scheduled windows (start/end) per contract. Any incidents that fall wholly within a registered window are excluded from the interactive latency SLO and are evaluated against the batch SLO. Partial overlaps are prorated by overlapping minutes.

3) Monthly credit accounting: calculate credits separately for the interactive and batch SLOs. Credits for batch SLO shortfalls are applied to a dedicated "batch offset bucket" with its own cap (we propose 10% of monthly plan spend as an initial cap for CloudForge). Interactive SLO credits follow the standard monthly credit ladder in the master template.

4) Canary & measurement period: recommend a 60-day canary post-signature where monitoring tags for "registered-scheduled-window" are validated. During canary the credit cap is halved.

5) Fallback behavior: when batch jobs cause resource contention, Redwood will attempt model-routing fallback to an alternate compatible model variant (no guaranteed identical latency). We will document fallback semantics in the Appendices.

Example (from attached spreadsheet):
- Month spend: €120,000
- Registered nightly window: 02:00-04:00 UTC (60 days on file)
- Observed batch P90 misses in a month: 3 hours total -> prorated credit of X (see spreadsheet)
- Proposed batch offset bucket cap: €12,000 (10%)

Next steps: if this approach sounds acceptable, I can loop in Marcus (legal) to produce redline language and Laura (product) to confirm runtime routing/telemetry needs. Would you prefer a single clause in the main SLA or an Appendix for the batch carveout?

Best,
Sofia
